documents.title: Anthropic sued for infringing neural network technology patents (Reuters, via The Star)
University of Tennessee sues Anthropic over neural network patents
University of Tennessee Research Foundation v. Anthropic PBC, 1:26-cv-00887

legal.name: University of Tennessee Research Foundation v. Anthropic PBC
legal.court: U.S. District Court, District of Delaware (1:26-cv-00887)
legal.status: Complaint filed with a jury demand; no ruling found as of 30 October 2026
legal.summary: The foundation that licenses the University of Tennessee's patents says Anthropic's AI systems infringe two of its patents on neuroscience-inspired machine learning, and asks for damages and an order to stop. Reported as the first patent case against Anthropic. Not among the matters this file took from the S-1.

evidence.quote: The University of Tennessee Research Foundation's complaint, filed on Monday and made public on Tuesday, said that Anthropic's AI systems violate its patents on machine-learning technology inspired by neuroscience.
It asked the court for an unspecified amount of monetary damages and an order blocking Anthropic from infringing its patents.
COMPLAINT filed with Jury Demand against Anthropic PBC

Bloomberg Law reported that the asserted patents are numbered 10,019,470 and 10,095,718, and that the complaint singles out Claude Code, Anthropic’s agentic coding tool, along with its underlying software architecture.
